segments.text: The climate of our planet has been changing rapidly since the industrial revolution.
The global average temperature has already risen by about 1.1 degrees.
One of the main causes is the emission of carbon dioxide produced by the burning of fossil fuels.
Deforestation and agricultural practices are all so deeply involved as a result of sea levels rise.
Floods and droughts have become more frequent
And typhoons have grown stronger than ever before
Bacal systems are being destroyed
And many species are facing
The threat of extinction
In 1997, the Kyoto Protocol was adopted
And each country was given a target
for the reduction of greenhouse gases In 2015, the Paris Agreement was reached
And the world set its goal of keeping the rise in temperature within 1.5 degrees
Each country has begun to increase investment in renewable energy
and to regulate emissions from cars and factories
But climate change is no longer a problem
That one country can solve by itself
Without international cooperation
We cannot protect the future of the Earth
The achievement of a sustainable society
Is now a shared goal across generations
